subject: Onramp commitments & SLO concessions — MAP and close timeline
messages:
From: Claire Wong <claire.wong@acmehealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Peters <tom.peters@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft & SLO ask for pilot — need clarity before exec review

Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're aligned on the value the model brings to triage workflows, but the exec team needs a clear mutual action plan and a tied set of commercial concessions (discount / ramp commitments) before we present to procurement next week. Two items we need from you to move to approval: 

1) A one-page MAP with milestones and acceptance criteria for the pilot (30-day pilot -> production ramp).
2) A clear statement of what SLA/latency SLO concessions Redwood can grant during ramp, and what commercial credits or discount tiers are tied to missed SLOs or missed ramp dates.

Can you share a draft MAP and an example of how pricing/discounts map to commits (e.g., commit to X qps / spend, receive Y% off after ramp)? We want to avoid open-ended language in the procurement packet.

Quick timeline: exec review Tue 29 Jun; procurement will aim to issue LOI by 02 Jul if we have clear terms.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Wong
Director, Clinical Ops | Acme Health
Mobile: (415) 555-0134

Attachment: "request_checklist.xlsx" (spreadsheet stub)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Claire Wong <claire.wong@acmehealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft & SLO ask for pilot — need clarity before exec review

Claire —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've attached a draft MAP and an SLA appendix that ties specific commercial concessions to milestones. High level summary below; full MAP attached (MAP_AcmeHealth_v2.pdf).

Summary highlights:
- Pilot: 30 days (proof of concept), acceptance = 3 production-like prompts sets passing latency and quality gates.
- Ramp: 0-2 months post-acceptance to reach agreed commit (target: 200 qps peak, average 40 qps sustained).
- Pricing/discount ladder: 0-30 days = eval credits (no commit). On go-live, commit to tier A (monthly commit $X) => 12% discount; Tier B (larger commit) => 20% discount after 60 days of sustained utilization.
- SLO concessions: For the pilot, we can guarantee 99.5% availability and 200ms p95 latency for single-region hosted endpoints. For production ramp, we can offer a temporary SLO of 99.0% with a latency objective of 250ms p95 for the first 60 days while we allocate dedicated capacity.
- Credits for SLO misses: If production availability drops below the committed SLO in a billing month, we offer a pro-rated credit tied to impacted token volume (example table in appendix).

We see three immediate asks for your procurement packet: the MAP PDF, the SLA appendix (SLA_Redwood-Acme_Appendix.docx), and a short note on the fallback policy (automatic fallback to a slightly older model variant to preserve availability).

I'm looping in Monica (commercial lead) and Marcus (solutions) to confirm sizing and the technical acceptance criteria. Do you want us to lock the Tier A numbers now, or propose a conditional LOI that pins the discount to the ramp performance?

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
Office: (650) 555-2120

Attachments: MAP_AcmeHealth_v2.pdf (PDF stub); SLA_Redwood-Acme_Appendix.docx (docx stub)

From: Tom Peters <tom.peters@acmehealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Claire Wong <claire.wong@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft & SLO ask for pilot — need clarity before exec review

Vivek / Monica —

Quick clarifying notes from procurement after an initial read: 
- The execs want hard numbers in the MAP for the ramp windows (end dates) and explicit triggers for discounts. "Conditional LOI" language is fine if it includes firm trigger conditions.
- For SLOs we need escalation commitments (who to notify, response SLAs for incidents impacting SLO) and a primary contact for post-sale operations.
- Please provide an example credit calculation for a missed latency SLO (short table is fine).

If you can send an updated MAP with these elements by EOD Mon (28 Jun) we'll include it in the packet for Tue's exec review.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Peters
VP, Procurement | Acme Health

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Tom Peters <tom.peters@acmehealth.com>, Claire Wong <claire.wong@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft & SLO ask for pilot — need clarity before exec review

Tom / Claire —

Thanks — sending a tighter MAP and the credit example now. Key callouts in this version (also attached):

- Ramp dates: Pilot start 2027-06-30, acceptance by 2027-07-30, production ramp complete by 2027-09-15. These are set against target traffic levels in the MAP.
- Discount triggers: 12% discount on committed spend after production acceptance and 60 days sustained usage at >= 80% of committed average qps. Escalation to 20% discount if they move to an annual committed contract at Year 1.
- SLO escalation: Page 3 of the appendix lists escalation steps: 15-minute incident acknowledgement, 2-hour mitigation window for P1 impact, weekly RCA cadence for sustained hits.
- Credit calculation: example row: If p95 latency > 250ms for > 2% of requests in a billing month => 5% invoice credit for the impacted month; >5% => 12% credit. (Detailed table in the attached doc.)

We'll also include a single-paragraph fallback policy that we can put into the LOI: automatic model variant fallback plus pre-authorized burst capacity for first 30 days of ramp.

If that aligns, we can prepare a conditional LOI that pins the 12% discount to the acceptance + 60-day utilization trigger; LOI would also reference the SLA appendix and credit table.

Monica Patel
Principal Commercial Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: updated_MAP_AcmeHealth_v2.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Claire Wong <claire.wong@acmehealth.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Peters <tom.peters@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft & SLO ask for pilot — need clarity before exec review

Monica / Vivek —

This is helpful — the execs liked the deterministic triggers. One quick ask: can you make the credit table explicit about how token volume is measured and whether retries/timeouts are excluded? Procurement flagged that as a common ambiguity.

Also please include the named post-sale contact for day-2 operations (we prefer an email alias).

If you can send a final package (MAP PDF, SLA appendix, sample credit calc, and LOI draft language) by EOD Tue we can move to LOI/Procurement.

Thanks — Claire

Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Final MAP package for exec packet — conditional LOI language included

Claire / Tom —

Attached is the final package for your exec packet: MAP_AcmeHealth_v2.pdf and SLA_Redwood-Acme_Appendix.docx. Highlights and clarifications per your asks: 

- Token measurement: We will measure billed token volume as successful responses returned by Redwood API (retries and timed-out requests excluded). The appendix defines the exact metric and the telemetry query used for verification.
- Credit example: If p95 latency > 250ms for >2% of successful requests in a month => 5% invoice credit for impacted month; >5% => 12% credit. Credits are pro-rated to impacted token volume.
- Post-sale contact: ops-oncall@redwood.ai (primary), ops-esc@redwood.ai (escalation).
- Conditional LOI excerpt: "Redwood and Acme agree that the 12% committed discount (Tier A) will be applied upon Production Acceptance and sustained utilization at >=80% of committed average qps for 60 continuous days. Failure to meet the utilization trigger within 120 days of Production Acceptance reverts pricing to standard self-serve rates until commit is re-established or replaced by an annual contract."

If this looks good I can have legal prepare a short LOI with those bullets and the SLA appendix referenced. I'll also open a HubSpot deal stage to capture the LOI and DocuSign flow.

Vivek
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_AcmeHealth_v2.pdf; SLA_Redwood-Acme_Appendix.docx
